top.title: Tech sell-off eases as stock market support measures are deployed after AI slump – business live
top.summary: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news Outsourcing group Capita has halved in value (!) in early trading, after the company announced the departure of its CEO, cut its profit forecasts, and proposed raising £190m in fresh capital. In a classic kitchen sink job, Capita told the City: Adolfo Hernandez has agreed to step down as chief executive officer and as a member of the Board with immediate effect. Adjusted operating profit in 2027 is expected to be £85m - £95m lower than previously expected, due to additional costs in relation to the Civil Service Pension Scheme contract, and “short-term contract headwinds” It is proposing to launch an equity raise of approximately £190m in the first half of 2027, “to reduce leverage and to allow the business to move forward from a more stable foundation” “It has been a privilege to lead Capita through this phase of its transformation. Three years ago we set out to turn Capita into a technology led, AI-enabled business services company. I am proud of the groundwork we have laid and the progress we have made under my leadership. Of course, within that I recognise that we have not delivered the service that members of the Civil Service Pension Scheme deserve. I am nevertheless overall especially proud of the contribution our people make every day to public services relied on by millions of citizens. Continue reading...

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.summary: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...

Culture.title: The Boy and the Suit of Lights review – a sensitive portrait of an aspiring toreador in a changing Spain
Culture.summary: Encouraged by his grandfather and single mother, the teen Borja dreams of a career that will end his family’s poverty, but the protesters are gathering strength Where last year’s bullfighting documentary Afternoons of Solitude by Albert Serra was a tightly trussed formalistic affair concerned by the question of style in the arena and in art, this Scottish-produced film is a looser, more social-realist approach to la corrida . Swerving a portrayal of the butchery itself, it focuses on the wider community significance of this tradition in the eastern Spanish city of Castellón, via the figure of aspiring teen toreador Borja. Supported by his harried, cigarillo-smoking single mother, Raquel, Borja hopes that wearing the sequined “suit of lights” will help lift his family out of poverty. Everything in his vicinity seems to point in the direction of the bullring: the Playmobil corrida he stages with his little brother, Erik, the mechanical rodeo bulls they ride at the fairground, the lessons in handling the muleta – the red cloth – he gets from grandfather, Matias, whose own bullfighting ambitions were scotched at an early age. But, as the protesters piling into the arena one day highlight, the bell may already be tolling for the kid’s chosen profession. Continue reading...
